title: Transport of tensor-composition coherence along compatible functor isomorphisms
statement: Let A, B, C be categories with bifunctors TA:A×A→A, TB:B×B→B, TC:C×C→C. Let F,F′:A→B, G,G′:B→C, H,H′:A→C be functors with isomorphisms eF:F≅F′, eG:G≅G′, eH:H≅H′. Give each functor a comparison from pullback of tensor to tensor of pullbacks, and let a:H≅F⋙G and b:F′⋙G′≅H′ be compositors. Assume each individual comparison square for eF,eG,eH commutes, a followed by the whiskered eF,eG equals eH followed by b⁻¹, and the primed comparisons satisfy tensor-composition coherence with b. Then the unprimed comparisons satisfy tensor-composition coherence with a. No monoidal associativity, unit, or symmetry structures are needed.

source.place: Naturality and inverse-compositor cancellation in Tags 07A4 and 07A7; the categorical substitution step of lem-sf-published-system-tensor-composition.

proof.text: Whisker eG on the left by F and eF on the right by G′ to form D:F⋙G≅F′⋙G′. Naturality of eG and of the second primed tensor comparison, together with the eF and eG comparison squares, proves the composite comparison square for D.

Postcompose the desired equation with the tensor square of D followed by b, which is invertible. The compositor-identification square and primed coherence identify its left side with eH on the tensor followed by the third primed comparison. The third comparison square identifies this with the right side; cancel the invertible postcomposition.

proof_origin.place: Categorical transport of the comparison diagram in Tags 07A4 and 07A7; explicit naturality/cancellation proof by U2.

theorem transfer_tensor_composition
    {A B C : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] [Category C]
    (TA : A × A ⥤ A) (TB : B × B ⥤ B) (TC : C × C ⥤ C)
    (F F' : A ⥤ B) (G G' : B ⥤ C) (H H' : A ⥤ C)
    (eF : F ≅ F') (eG : G ≅ G') (eH : H ≅ H')
    (mF : TA ⋙ F ≅ F.prod F ⋙ TB) (mG : TB ⋙ G ≅ G.prod G ⋙ TC)
    (mH : TA ⋙ H ≅ H.prod H ⋙ TC)
    (nF : TA ⋙ F' ≅ F'.prod F' ⋙ TB) (nG : TB ⋙ G' ≅ G'.prod G' ⋙ TC)
    (nH : TA ⋙ H' ≅ H'.prod H' ⋙ TC)
    (a : H ≅ F ⋙ G) (b : F' ⋙ G' ≅ H')
    (hmF : ∀ M N, eF.hom.app (TA.obj (M, N)) ≫ nF.hom.app (M, N) =
      mF.hom.app (M, N) ≫ TB.map
        (Prod.mkHom (eF.hom.app M) (eF.hom.app N)))
    (hmG : ∀ M N, eG.hom.app (TB.obj (M, N)) ≫ nG.hom.app (M, N) =
      mG.hom.app (M, N) ≫ TC.map
        (Prod.mkHom (eG.hom.app M) (eG.hom.app N)))
    (hmH : ∀ M N, eH.hom.app (TA.obj (M, N)) ≫ nH.hom.app (M, N) =
      mH.hom.app (M, N) ≫ TC.map
        (Prod.mkHom (eH.hom.app M) (eH.hom.app N)))
    (ha : ∀ M, a.hom.app M ≫ eG.hom.app (F.obj M) ≫
      G'.map (eF.hom.app M) = eH.hom.app M ≫ b.inv.app M)
    (hc : ∀ M N, G'.map (nF.hom.app (M, N)) ≫
      nG.hom.app (F'.obj M, F'.obj N) ≫
      TC.map (Prod.mkHom (b.hom.app M) (b.hom.app N)) =
      b.hom.app (TA.obj (M, N)) ≫ nH.hom.app (M, N)) :
    ∀ M N, a.hom.app (TA.obj (M, N)) ≫ G.map (mF.hom.app (M, N)) ≫
      mG.hom.app (F.obj M, F.obj N) = mH.hom.app (M, N) ≫
      TC.map (Prod.mkHom (a.hom.app M) (a.hom.app N))
